brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four bases in a row (piece:0..3,0,0), each with a soil-filled hex-bin-third-drain bin planted with a seedling.

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: Irrigation run run:run-1 at level 0, going straight in through the outer face of (0,0) and through (1,0), (2,0) and (3,0). The configurator accepted it.

The pipe passes under all four bins and each bin has drain holes. The configurator only checks fit, so whether water actually reaches the soil, and whether the pipe and bins hold water, isn't checked.

finish.summary: I built a four-cell planter: four full bases in a straight row from (0,0,0) to (3,0,0), with one irrigation pipe run (run-1) laid straight through all four bases. It enters at the outer face of the first cell. Because the pipe passes through each base, every cell can only take a third-depth bin, so each one holds a hex-bin-third-drain bin. I filled the bins with soil and planted basil, mint, parsley and chives seedlings, which are only there to show the use. The open faces are capped (the pipe entry face is left open) and the three joints between bases are bolted. The configurator checks reported no errors, no prop warnings and no mesh collisions. The design comes to 30 parts, about 1,838 g of filament and about 2,708 minutes of printing. The configurator only checks fit. It can't confirm that the pipe or bins hold water or that water actually reaches the soil.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes

outcomes.message: dryRun is for addProp, moveProp and plant; other ops answer in the same time by being applied and undone.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.
